ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in Figure 31, given \(I = 5\text{A}\), \(U_1 = 20\text{V}\), and \(R_2\) absorbs power of \(25\text{W}\), the total voltage \(U\) is ___ V.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, on the left side are the two terminals of the total voltage U, with the upper terminal marked “+” and the lower terminal marked “-”. The current I goes from the upper terminal along the wire to the right and enters the right-side branch. The right-side branch, from top to bottom, is R1, R2, and a 2Ω resistor in sequence, and the three are connected in series. R1 has U1 marked across its two ends, with polarity upper positive and lower negative. Reasoning: In a series circuit, R1, R2, and the 2Ω resistor have the same current I = 5 A flowing through them. It is known that U1 = 20 V. R2 absorbs power 25 W, therefore according to the passive sign convention, its voltage drop is V2 = P/I = 25/5 = 5 V. The voltage drop across the 2Ω resistor is V3 = I·R = 5×2 = 10 V. The total voltage U is equal to the sum of the voltage drops of each part in series: U = U1 + V2 + V3 = 20 + 5 + 10 = 35 V.
